transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

My body just feels out of my control. At first I was pacing around my apartment all night, making notes for a supper club, and lately I’m so slowed down my sister says it takes me forever just to put my shoes on.
How many days in a row did that period of high energy and little need for sleep last before you started slowing down?
It’s been about four months altogether, since I got fired from the restaurant.
During that time when you were pacing and full of energy, did you ever see, hear, or believe things that others didn't, like hearing voices or feeling you had special powers or a special mission?

I didn’t hear voices or anything, but I really believed I was going to build the best bilingual supper club in the city. I thought investors would be stupid not to back me, even though I didn’t have a job or any money lined up.
During this slowed-down period, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living?
I’m not sure. I’ve been feeling really low and stuck, but I don’t really know what counts as those kinds of thoughts.

Right now, during this slowed-down period, are you still noticing any bursts of high energy, racing thoughts, or grand ideas mixed in with the low, stuck feelings, or do you feel purely down and slowed without any of that energized feeling?
Yeah, I still get racing thoughts sometimes. My mind starts jumping from recipes to logos, then investors, then renting a space—each idea leads to three more, and I can’t sleep.

When you notice the racing thoughts and jumping ideas, are they happening at the very same time as the slowed-down, low feelings, or do they come in separate stretches where you feel one way and then the other?

It’s kind of at the same time. I feel low and stuck, but then my mind is still jumping—recipes, logos, investors, finding a space—and it just keeps multiplying. I can’t sleep because every idea leads to a few more.
